questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating Left and Right Limits at an Interior Point
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13932295/assets/e489437aa3b22a90d71dea3d30ff7a53bb800580775666f97dd4a6cf2db76e6d.png)

The figure above shows the graphs of the functions $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x).$

Current part:

Find ${lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{-}}g(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{+}}g(x).$ If a limit does not exist, write "DNE" (without the quotation marks).

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{-}}g(x)=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}                
                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                                

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{+}}g(x)=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-2}}
questions.worked_solution:
As $x$ approaches $-1$ from the left, the function $g(x)$ approaches $2.$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{-}}g(x)=2.
$$

Likewise, as $x$ approaches $-1$ from the right, the function $g(x)$ approaches $0.$ Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{+}}g(x)=0.
$$

In conclusion, we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{-}}g(x)=2,\,{lim}_{x\to \,(-1)^{+}}g(x)=0.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
From the graph, we see that as we approach $x=2$ from the left, the $y$-value approaches $-1.$ So the left-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}g(x)=-1.
$$

Similarly, when we approach $x=2$ from the right, the $y$-value again approaches $-1.$ So the right-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}g(x)=-1.
$$

 

Since both the left and right-hand limits exist and are equal to $-1,$ we conclude that

 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)=-1.
$$

questions.worked_solution:

Consequently, $g(x)$ approaches the value $3$ as $x$ approaches $-\infty ,$ and we have

$$
{lim}_{x\to -\infty }g(x)=3.
$$

On the right side of the graph, as the values of $x$ increase and approach $\infty ,$ the graph of the function decrease without bound to $-\infty .$   Therefore,

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }g(x)=-\infty .
$$

questions.worked_solution:
According to the sum and constant multiple rules, we can compute the required limit as follows:

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,2}(7f(x)+8g(x)-2{x}^{3})=7{lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)+8{lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)-2{lim}_{x\to \,2}{x}^{3}
$$

  

The above equation assumes that ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)$ and ${lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)$ both exist.

In part 5, we found that ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=4,$ and from part 3, we found ${lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)=-1.$ So, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,2}(7f(x)+8g(x)-2{x}^{3}) & =7{lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)+8{lim}_{x\to \,2}g(x)-2{lim}_{x\to \,2}{x}^{3} \\  & =7\cdot 4+8\cdot (-1)-2\cdot {2}^{3} \\  & =28-8-16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
